task_types.B: semantically overlapping tool choices -- multiple tools plausibly relevant, one clearly best
task_types.C: ambiguous natural language -- underspecified request, several reasonable interpretations
task_types.D: multi-tool task -- answering fully requires more than one tool call
task_types.E: unsupported operation -- a mutation or a capability this server does not expose; correct answer is to say so, not to call a WRITE-shaped or nonexistent tool
task_types.F: guidance-vs-READ ambiguity -- could plausibly be answered by a guidance tool or by a specific READ tool
task_types.G: phrased the way an ordinary (non-technical-vocabulary) pfSense operator would actually ask, not in tool-schema language

notes: Every `expected_tools` entry is the primary, independently-reviewed correct answer. `acceptable_tools` (when present) lists additional tool(s) that would also be a reasonable, non-wrong first choice for the same request (used for a looser 'eventual/acceptable' scoring pass, never for 'first-choice-correct' scoring). No task prompt names an MCP tool. No task is satisfiable by, or expects, a WRITE-shaped call.
